title: Corrugated cellulose fibre wall cladding on a 17-year-old house: code compliance certificate refused
jurisdiction: New Zealand (MBIE Chief Executive determination; Building Act 2004; comparative only, not Alberta)
code_edition: NZ Building Code in force when the house was constructed (per decision); B2, E2 and E3 cited; edition not stated

facts.text: A 17-year-old three-bedroom detached house, three storeys in part, on a south-sloping excavated coastal site in a medium wind zone, with complex junctions and a moderate to high weathertightness risk.

Wall claddings are generally corrugated cellulose fibre, with some areas of weatherboard and fibre-cement sheet; the corrugated sheet is bitumen-impregnated cellulose fibre with a pigmented resin finish.
The matter relates primarily to weathertightness of the corrugated cellulose fibre wall cladding; the owners had commissioned a performance assessment that the authority declined to accept.
Figure 1 is an approximate layout of the house (p.3).
